content: The Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.), derived from the Latin term Scientiæ Baccalaureus, is an undergraduate academic degree awarded upon the successful completion of a program of study that typically spans three to five years, depending on the country and institution. For example, in economics, a B.Sc. may include additional supporting courses such as statistics. This degree is also commonly awarded in professional fields like engineering, journalism, accounting, and advertising. In some cases, a Bachelor of Science degree is granted in disciplines traditionally associated with arts degrees, such as literature, while other institutions, like the Oxbridge universities, predominantly award arts qualifications. These distinctions are often rooted in historical and traditional practices. The designation B.Sc. (Hons) is used to indicate an honors degree, which typically involves a higher level of academic achievement. Historically, in some regions, the B.Sc. was considered a postgraduate degree. In Brazil, the Bachelor of Science degree is a graduation-level qualification that includes a mandatory one-year probationary period at the end of the program. This is followed by comprehensive written and oral evaluations, known as Monografia. The typical duration for completing a Bachelor of Science degree varies by country. In many nations, such as Australia, Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, India, and South Africa, the degree generally takes three years to complete. In some cases, such as in England, it may extend to four years if a one-year industry placement is included. In other countries, such as Canada (outside Quebec), Ireland, Japan, South Korea, and the United States, the degree typically requires four years of study. In certain regions, such as Chile and Egypt, the program may extend to five years, often including a research thesis in the final year.
